value: A domestic golden-retriever world where small incidents can become grand dramas: stolen balls, contested furniture, treats, garden gates and river adventures are treated with exaggerated stakes, dry humour and genuine affection.
tiny domestic stakes versus apocalyptic storytelling
repetition and obsession versus the fleeting nature of reward

name: Doja
summary: An independent, self-assured, calculating golden retriever with princess-like entitlement and mischievous gremlin behaviour. She wants control over her surroundings, attention and possessions.
habits: Patrols and monitors the household or garden.
Secures attention and scratches on her terms.
Steals or barters with balls and other prized objects.
Winds Bam Bam up and enjoys provoking a reaction.
Has exuberant wet zoomies and digs after river visits.
Nudges an arm for attention or a witness to her activities.
narrative_voice: Wry, commanding, dismissive, sly or melodramatically outraged.

name: Bam Bam
summary: A large fluffy, affectionate, eager-to-please retriever whose life revolves around tennis balls and his people. He is gentle, emotionally sensitive, patient and comically single-minded rather than truly unintelligent.
habits: Searches for, retrieves and mourns tennis balls.
Waits patiently for play and approval.
Carries objects in a gentle, controlled mouth grip.
Leaves slobber and puts his enormous paws everywhere.
Responds enthusiastically to the possibility of another throw.
narrative_voice: Earnest, repetitive, hopeful, sometimes grandly tragic about trivial losses.
recurring_grudge: Teddy is singled out as an object of Bam's inexplicable hostility in some songs.
avoid: Mistaking his single-mindedness for a lack of feelings

name: Mama
role: Human caregiver and central source of comfort, affection, treats and attention.
narrative_use: Can act as the loving authority, witness, mediator or dispenser of rewards.
notes: Do not invent a fixed physical description or personal biography.

name: Teddy
role: Named target of Bam Bam's recurring comically disproportionate hostility.
notes: Teddy's species, identity and motive for the feud are not fixed here; preserve ambiguity.
narrative_use: A recurring punchline or unexpected source of tension.

name: Johnny Three Fridges
role: Named subject of an established song family.
setting_reference: Minnesota is connected with Johnny in prior song-writing context.
notes: The three fridges are part of the character's name; do not invent their origin as canon.

name: Moses
role: Central figure in a musical tongue-twister and wordplay song.
notes: The wordplay is established; a stable wider character biography is not.

description: Shared domestic territory with coveted furniture, people, treats, gates and space for play.
Site of wet adventures, digging and zoomies; in dramatic songs water becomes a threatening force that swallows or carries away balls.
The boundary between possession and loss, safety and adventure; a ball beyond it becomes a quest.

name: New Mills
description: Recurring named destination celebrated in song, often elevated to an outsized anthem.

name: The Golden Court
description: Mock-royal lens through which golden-retriever household hierarchy can be dramatized.
notes: Title exists; exact institutions and membership are not fixed.

meaning: Doja's territory, comfort and claimed sovereignty.
Bam Bam's physical comedy and affectionate disregard for neatness.

idea: The ball is found, thrown, lost, grieved and pursued again. The cycle itself can be funny, heroic or existential.
Doja's strategic control clashes with Bam's trusting enthusiasm, producing conflict without removing their bond.
A small event in a dog's day is narrated as war, divine judgement, royal intrigue or Greek tragedy.
Chairs, balls, gates, attention and personal space are contested.
Mock-monarchy, coronations, self-importance and royal dignity applied to golden retrievers.
Beneath the absurdity lies genuine attachment, loyalty and grief at things lost.
Tongue-twisters, repetition, absurd logic, escalating refrains and deliberately clumsy language.
Furniture, clutter, unwelcome objects and household frustrations acquire outsized comic significance.
Familiar places and ordinary figures receive extravagant anthems and mythic treatment.
